A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IPDreamer. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison. Renamed and relocated material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v4 reports original 3D-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and an 80-participant user study, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v6 reports original generation results, quantitative comparisons, user preferences, and ablations, including retained experiments and new challenging-prompt and multiple-image examples.

M1.justification: The core geometry, texture, masked-attention, and local/global optimization procedures survive the IPSD-to-IPSDS and LEPI-to-Mask-guided Compositional Alignment renaming. Much of v6 Section 3.3 already appears in v4 Appendix F.3. The substantive adaptation accepts multiple separate reference images through this alignment procedure; v6 also omits the auxiliary joint IPSD/Zero-1-to-3 optimization variant from v4 Appendix D.

E1.justification: v6 retains the original 20 textual prompts and adds ten challenging prompts, including leaves flying in the wind, ripples, and splashing waves, targeting generation without a clear principal subject. Figure 6(b) adds composition from multiple separate reference images. Conversely, the dedicated single-image reconstruction experiments in v4 Appendix D are absent. These change the evaluated input conditions and task coverage.

E2.justification: v6 Tables 1–2 add LRM and LGM to DreamFusion, Magic3D, Fantasia3D, and ProlificDreamer in the quantitative comparison and user study. Meanwhile, the evaluated Zero-1-to-3 and SyncDreamer comparisons in v4 Appendices D–E disappear, although their citations remain. ProlificDreamer/VSD in the new challenging-prompt illustrations is an existing comparator.

E3.justification: The quantitative evaluation expands from 20 to 30 prompts. The user study now samples 16 prompts from the larger pool and compares six baselines, retaining 80 volunteers and 1,280 comparisons. v6 Figure 6(b) introduces a control that holds the coarse model and reference images fixed while swapping localization labels. Metrics and optimization budgets remain unchanged; the delta_geo ablation references the revised prompt pool without establishing whether it was rerun.

E4.justification: The geometry-guidance, delta_geo, and qualitative LEPI ablations are retained under new numbering and terminology. v6 adds the localization-label swapping case in Figure 6(b), but removes the quantitative LEPI validation in v4 Table 5 and the Zero-1-to-3-only versus combined-loss artifact analysis in Figure 13. This substantially changes the evidence testing alignment and integration effectiveness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-generation run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both report user-preference percentages without uncertainty estimates; adding comparator rows does not change that practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 reports replacement results on the expanded prompt set: IPDreamer's FID/CLIP scores change from 257.17/0.2859 to 253.32/0.2716, which is not a same-setting performance comparison. v6 adds LRM/LGM results, including 70.27%/65.48% preference for IPDreamer, and new challenging-prompt and composition outputs. v4 Table 5 and Figures 13–15 disappear. The four original user-preference rows and delta_geo scores of 0.8228/0.8389 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The core mathematical definitions and optimization gradients remain equivalent after renaming and relocation; v4 Appendix F.3 Equations 15–21 correspond to v6 Equations 11–17. v6 removes the coarse Zero-1-to-3 gradient in v4 Equation 2 and the combined-loss definitions in Appendix D, Equations 12–14. These are limited removals of auxiliary formulations; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The appearance-control claim remains, but v6's introduction, contribution list, and conclusion elevate composition from multiple diverse images into a central capability. The introduction additionally claims successful generation for ambiguous or unclear-subject prompts where existing text-to-3D and image-to-3D methods fail. This substantively broadens the claimed contribution beyond v4's emphasis on complex-reference appearance transfer and reference/NeRF mismatch.

C2.justification: v6 replaces the introduction's explanation based on VSD's LoRA-training randomness with one based on insufficient appearance information in text. It interprets the new localization-label experiment as evidence of compositional diversity. It also removes v4 Appendix G's specific qualifications about imperfect appearance/color matching and deployment speed, while retaining the main explanations of image guidance and alignment.

D1.justification: v6 no longer documents the explicit Zero-1-to-3 initialization, DMTet mesh extraction, and DPT normal-estimation recipe given in v4's method section. It also drops the blanket LEPI-off-unless-indicated statement and the user study's text-only image-generation clarification. Hardware, optimization steps, timestep schedules, memory, batch size, rendering resolution, and code-link disclosure remain. GPT-4v, SAM, and ControlNet preprocessing details largely move from Appendix F.3 into Section 3.3.

R1.justification: v6 adds Hong et al.'s LRM and Tang et al.'s LGM references and incorporates them into its comparisons. References to InstantID, DPT, and DMTet are removed. The diffusion-model, controllable-generation, and 3D-generation related-work discussions otherwise remain substantially similar; citation-style and author-name formatting changes are not new research positioning.

P1.justification: v6 substantially rewrites the introduction and conclusion, reorganizes the method around IPSDS and compositional alignment instead of explicit NeRF/mesh stages, and brings detailed LEPI training into the main text. Experiments are reorganized around single and multiple complex images, terminology shifts from texture editing toward object generation, and the appendix hierarchy is extensively restructured.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is comprehensively redrawn around mesh optimization and masked attention. Figures 1 and 6 gain panels, and the main qualitative comparison is rebuilt using material from v4 Figure 12 alongside revised and new outputs. Table 1 is transposed; user-study results and localization-mask visualization move into the main text. Several supplementary displays are removed, and the document adopts a different title, header, and citation layout.

improvement.justification: v6 more directly tests its broadened claims through challenging prompts, LRM/LGM comparisons, and multiple-image composition, while making the alignment procedure easier to find. However, it removes quantitative validation of that central component in v4 Table 5, explicit appearance and speed limitations, and useful initialization and normal-estimation details. Broader evidence and clearer focus coexist with weaker reproducibility and qualification of claims, leaving the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
